title: Type-removal responses reveal another member's private draft use
description: An authenticated household member can try to remove a shared object or relationship type that has no saved use. A definition_in_use response reveals that another private draft references or edits the selected type; a successful proposal indicates that blocker is absent. This is a type-specific private-draft predicate without exposing names or values.
claimed_root_cause: The deletion guard uses other members' private draft records to choose an externally visible success or definition_in_use response.

trace.description: An authenticated member proposes deletion of a known shared type.
The member's draft and content version are checked before evaluating the type proposal.
Deletion invokes assertUnused; relationship type proposal applies the same guard.
The guard reads other owners' drafts and checks references and edits to the selected type.
Caller receives distinguishable definition_in_use if another draft uses the type.

evidence.description: Query selects household drafts whose userId differs from caller.
Object-type branch tests other drafts and throws definition_in_use; relationship branch mirrors this.
Ordinary map reads select only caller's draft, establishing separate private boundary.
A test asserts another member's pending type edit produces definition_in_use.
Integration test checks private names and values are absent while type-specific rejection remains visible.

blockers: The intended privacy contract does not specify whether another member's use of a shared type in a private draft is confidential metadata.
The required OS sandbox lacks verified total scratch disk limits and race-safe artifact promotion, so a bounded two-member check was not run.

validation_plan.local: With the required sandbox, create a dummy household with two members and an otherwise unused shared type. Compare one member's deletion response before and after the other stages a private object or type edit using it; stop at the response-code difference. Have the product owner decide whether this metadata is intended to be public.
